rounds.text: Scan Steels Ltd carries significant valuation and fundamental risks that are unsupported by its recent price strength, trading at the absolute peak of its 52-week range and 0.0% away from its 52-week high [E47, E48]. A discounted cash flow model explicitly reveals that intrinsic value sits at Rs 42 per share against a higher market price of Rs 50.5, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -20.1% [E44, E45]. Fundamental profitability metrics remain severely depressed, highlighted by a multi-year median return on equity of just 4% to 6% and a 3-year low ROE of 4.50% [E26, E27, E28, E60]. Long-term top-line expansion is exceptionally weak, evidenced by a poor compounded sales growth of 2.75% over the past five years and a negative -8% growth rate over the last 3 years [E16, E59]. Furthermore, despite reporting repeated profits, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% and refuses to return capital to shareholders [E4, E58]. Borrowings have also ticked upward to Rs 72 Cr alongside a massive 105.0% surge in capital work-in-progress, adding execution and balance sheet risk as uncompleted projects scale up [E39, E40]. Conceded: the company demonstrates positive near-term momentum with an operating cash flow of Rs 37 Cr, a 1.85x cash conversion ratio, and a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.16x [E34, E35, E38].

Conceded: intrinsic value sits at Rs 42 against a market price of Rs 50.5 [E44, E45], and multi-year median return on equity is restricted to 4% to 6% [E26, E27, E28, E60]. However, the claim that the price sits at the absolute peak without support is contradicted by accelerating fundamentals, including a 51% compounded profit growth in the trailing twelve months and a 30% YoY net profit surge [E21, E63]. The multi-year sales weakness [E16, E59] ignores a robust 10% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a rules-based screen score of 74 out of 100 [E17, E61]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4, E58], but retained capital fuels internal expansion as demonstrated by a 105.0% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 41 Cr [E40]. Finally, rising borrowings to Rs 72 Cr [E39] are comfortably mitigated by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.16x and a stellar 1.85x cash conversion ratio backing profits with Rs 37 Cr in operating cash flow [E34, E35, E38].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 37 Cr with a 1.85x cash conversion backing reported profits [E34, E35], and capital work-in-progress expanded by 105.0% to Rs 41 Cr [E40]. However, pointing to TTM profit growth of 51% [E21] obscures a chronic historical malaise, evidenced by a 5-year compounded profit contraction of -7% [E19] and a 3-year compounded sales contraction of -8% [E16]. Conceded: the TTM sales growth is 10% [E17], but this single-period uptick does not erase a poor 5-year sales growth rate of 2.75% [E59] or an inconsistent operating-margin trend [E32]. Furthermore, citing a rules-based screen score of 74 [E61] ignores that the screen itself flags decelerating earnings growth and a low 5% ROE [E66, E67]. Finally, while debt-to-equity is low at 0.16x [E38], total borrowings still escalated to Rs 72 Cr [E39] while returns remain deeply depressed, with median 3-year ROE sitting stagnant at 5% [E28] and intrinsic value pegged below the current trading price at Rs 42 [E44, E45].
